text:
alex: Heads-up — I ran an nsys capture on a busy Dedicated pod and the timeline is noisy. Small kernels (bytecopy/dispatch) show up as the main hotblocks; suspect we don't have fine-grained NVTX around the batching/coalescer path so the kernel timeline attribution is misleading.

maria: Which config and workload? can you paste the nsys command and a short snip?

alex: ran on commit d3a2b4f, workload=chat-stream-heavy, 8xA10G. nsys cmd: `nsys profile -o run.d3 --trace=cuda,nvtx -t 10s -- ./bin/redwood_serving --workload chat-stream-heavy`

Here's a brief kernel dump from the capture (filtered):
```
# top kernels by GPU time
kv_dispatch_kernel     42.3%  
dispatch_small_kernel  18.4%
softmax_fused_kernel   12.1%
prefix_cache_lookup    8.9%
allreduce_async        6.5%
```

But the NVTX ranges we get are only at a coarse "request batch" level, so we can't tell whether the kv_dispatch time is per-request or due to coalesced batching merging many requests.

ryan: Right — we've historically had NVTX at the batch-enter/batch-exit granularity. For debugging that's fine, but for timeline-based hotspot attribution we really need per-request spans (or per-kvspan) plus consistent kernel naming so post-processing can unambiguously map ranges -> kernels.

Proposal I'm drafting: a naming convention of `req/<shortid>::stage/<name>::kern/<kernel>` where `<shortid>` is an 8-char hex of the request id. Examples: `req/7f3a2b1c::stage/prefetch::kern/kv_lookup`. This keeps names compact and parseable. Thoughts?

sam: I like parseable names. Concern: building these strings on the hot path allocates and can regress latency. We should avoid heap allocations and minimize syscalls. Options: 1) pre-allocated thread-local char buf reused, populated with snprintf; 2) numeric payloads using NVTX domain/payload fields (store a 64-bit tag = (req_hash<<32)|stage_id) and emit short static labels only once per run; 3) enable per-request NVTX only under a runtime flag/sampling.

maria: I pushed a tiny prototype to my branch that uses NVTX_RANGE_PUSH_EX with a static thread-local buffer to avoid allocs. Snippet: 
```
char tlbuf[64];
int n = snprintf(tlbuf, sizeof(tlbuf), "r:%08x|s:%02d|k:%s", shortid, stage_id, kernel_short);
nvtxEventAttributes_t attr = {0};
attr.version = NVTX_VERSION;
attr.size = NVTX_EVENT_ATTRIB_STRUCT_SIZE;
attr.messageType = NVTX_MESSAGE_TYPE_ASCII;
attr.message.asciiz = tlbuf;
nvtxRangePushEx(&attr);
```
This avoids heap allocs but still writes to the buffer on the hot path. I measured microbenchmarks — writes cost ~150ns per call on x86.

perfbot: Automated benchmark results for maria/prototype on dedicated-8: enabling full per-request NVTX (thread-local buffer) => median latency +0.8%, p99 +4.2%. Sampling it to 1/10 requests drops impact to median +0.1%, p99 +0.6%. Flag: `INSTRUMENT_PER_REQ=0` default.

alex: That reg is small but not zero. We should make per-request NVTX opt-in + sampling. Also we should provide a numeric-only fast-path where we only push a small integer tag via `nvtxRangePushA(static_labels[tag])` where `static_labels` is pre-allocated for the run and tag computed cheaply. Saves the snprintf cost at expense of a one-time label table prep.

ryan: Agree. Implementation plan:
1) Standardize naming: `req/<8hex>::stg/<short>::k/<kern>` as ascii names for traces when enabled.
2) Fast-path: runtime prepares a label pool for active (req,stage,kern) tuples but only when tracing is enabled (cheap map from uint32 tag -> char*). On hot path we emit `nvtxRangePushA(label_pool[tag])`.
3) Fallback: when no label exists (rare), push a short numeric-only domain marker and schedule label creation off the hot path.
4) Sampling & flagging: default off; `INSTRUMENT_PER_REQ` and `SAMPLE_PER_REQ=0.1` to preserve performance.

sam: Also we should strongly avoid emitting ranges inside very small kernels (sub-200ns). For those, rely on aggregation at the batch level. The instrumentation should be aware of kernel duration distribution. Possibly only emit per-request NVTX for kernels > 1us or when sampling hits.

maria: I'll open an RFC with the naming examples, the fast-path label pool design, and perf numbers. I'll include a `tracegen` script that can ingest the numeric tags and produce a mapping file so perf folks can reconstruct human readable traces offline.

alex: Action items: maria create RFC + prototype PR; ryan review label-pool API; sam add heuristics for kernel-duration thresholds; I'll run a 30-minute nsys sweep with the label pool approach and post timeline snapshots to #eng-runtime.

perfbot: Noted — CI perf harness will run maria/prototype baseline vs opt-in label-pool; alert if median reg >1% or p99 >3% on dedicated-8 smoke.

ryan: One last nit — name delimiting: use `::` between major parts and single `/` inside segments. It makes simple regex parsing easier: e.g. `^req/([0-9a-f]{8})::stg/([^:]+)::k/([^:]+)$`.

alex: perfect. Thanks team. I'll drop the nsys link + screenshots in the RFC. :thumbsup:
